A:eliza-catherine-stevenson.note: Her husband W. T. Andrews named her parents and their son James David in his 1912 autobiography. James David’s 1937 obituary independently names William Thomas and Eliza Stevenson Andrews as his parents.

A:william-thomas-andrews.note: In his 1912 autobiography he identifies his wife Eliza Catherine Stevenson, her parents James C. and Margaret C., and their son James David.

A:james-david-andrews.note: His father’s 1912 autobiography names him, and his 1937 Pulaski Citizen obituary names his parents and son Major General Frank M. Andrews. Nashville Public Library’s family papers identify Frank Maxwell Andrews as a son of James David and Lula Maxwell.

A:lula-adaline-maxwell.note: Nashville Public Library’s finding aid identifies Lula Adaline Maxwell Andrews and James D. Andrews as Frank Maxwell Andrews’s parents.

A:frank-maxwell-andrews.note: James David’s obituary names his son Major General Frank M. Andrews; Nashville Public Library’s family papers identify him as Frank Maxwell Andrews. W. T. Andrews’s own 1912 memoir names James David’s mother and grandparents, connecting this branch to Elam and Lydia Stevenson.

A:mary-dockery:newton.note: Mary Ann Dockery married Bailus Newton in 1867. The 1880 census records Balus Newton, wife Mary and a daughter Elizabeth, seven. An Alabama death index names Mary Marzee Dockery as the mother of Oda Verbena Newton, a possible match for the youngest child in the household.

MAT_WAYNE_W_LIVESAY.note: Locomotive engineer for Burlington Northern Santa Fe for 30 years, retiring in 2000 (Find a Grave memorial 108771556). Buried at McKnight Cemetery, Cushing.

MAT_BARBARA_PHILLIPS.note: Wayne’s Texas birth index names her as Barbara Phillips. Lester’s 2001 obituary identifies her as his deceased wife. A 2014 Pearland Historical Society notice identifies Carylon as daughter of Lester and Barbara and sister of Wayne. Barbara’s own parents and dates remain unverified. Her 1995 Panola Watchman obituary gives birth on 7 April 1918 in Nacogdoches, names her parents as Carl C. and Beulah Turner Phillips, and records her marriage to Lester W. Livesay on 21 April 1935 and her death on 2 September 1995 at Panola Nursing Home. The shared stone at Restland Memorial Park repeats the dates. The Texas birth index for Wayne also names her as Barbara Phillips.

MAT_LESTER_SR.note: The 1900 census lists Lester W. as a son in Floyd and Alice’s household; the matching 1920 household includes Sadah and Lester Jr. The census reports November 1894 but gives an age that does not agree with that month and year. The original Harris County marriage register records Lester W. Livesay and Sadah H. McCormick marrying on 10 October 1911, vol. 4, p. 402, handwritten no. 22072. Its margin notes a mother’s consent on file without naming her. His headstone at the Confederate Cemetery, Alvin, reads “Lester W., Nov. 8, 1894 – Aug. 8, 1989” on a double stone with Esther Voris (b. 1910 Alvin, d. 2005), his later wife; Find a Grave dates that marriage to 1942. The 1900 census lists Lester W. as a son in Floyd and Alice’s household; the matching 1920 household includes Sadah and Lester Jr. The original Harris County marriage register records Lester W. Livesay and Sadah H. McCormick marrying on 10 October 1911, vol. 4, p. 402, handwritten no. 22072. Its margin notes a mother’s consent on file without naming her; Lester was then 16.

MAT_SADAH_MCCORMICK.note: Probable identification with Sadah Livesay Vaughan in Texas death certificate 37586, naming informant Alice Livesay Kauitzsch. Certificate records birth 13 August 1893 in Anderson, Indiana, death 29 April 1978 in Houston, father J. T. McCormack and mother’s maiden name Unknown. Sarah H. McCormick/Frances household with daughter Sadie is a lead, not established identity; no full first-name expansion or mother’s maiden surname is proved. Parent links remain unresolved. MAT_LEMUEL_SANDRIDGE.note: Gravestone at Hochatown Cemetery (shared with Audrey): Lemuel Lamar, Dec. 4, 1911 – Mar. 13, 1979. His memorial gives Prescott, Nevada County, Arkansas, as birthplace and Dallas as place of death (not yet confirmed by an original record).

MAT_AUDREY_NELSON.note: The 1920 census identifies Audrey as daughter of household head William Nelson; Julia is listed in the household. A memorial reproduces an obituary naming her parents William and Julia Robbins. The obituary’s original publication remains to be located.

MAT_CLINTON_SANDRIDGE.note: The McCurtain Gazette of 20 December 1961 reports his death at home in Broken Bow that morning and names Lemuel as his son. It gives 25 September 1892 as his birth, conflicting with age 43 in the 1930 census (about 1886–1887). No birth year is selected while that discrepancy remains unresolved; his parents are unknown. Gravestone at Broken Bow Cemetery: Clinton L., Sept. 24, 1882 – Dec. 20, 1961, married Maggie June 19, 1910. The 1961 McCurtain Gazette printed 25 September 1892, and the 1930 census age (43) implies about 1887; the stone's 1882 is adopted with the conflict noted. The 1961 notice's birthplace “Burn” is probably Beirne, Clark County, Arkansas. Lead for parents: William D. Sandridge and Mary E. “Molly” Cole (married 8 October 1877; she died 1897 and is buried at Browns Cemetery, Beirne), per Find a Grave family links. The 1961 notice independently names brothers Lon and L. P., matching Lon P. Sandridge (1889–1974) on those links. No parent link added. First wife: Esther Margaret Bolls (died 1909).

MAT_MAGGIE_SANDRIDGE.note: Maggie is recorded as Lemuel’s mother in the 1930 census; her maiden name needs further confirmation. Gravestone at Broken Bow Cemetery: Maggie A., May 2, 1891 – July 15, 1982; married Clinton June 19, 1910. Lead: a Find a Grave memorial calls her Margaret Ann “Maggie” Cash, born at Prescott, Nevada County, Arkansas, daughter of James L. Cash (1863–1946) and Maxie Ann McClure Cash (1865–1941). This conflicts with the Texas birthplace in the 1930 census. The Cash maiden name and parents are unconfirmed by an original record.

W. Livesay did not know either parent’s name or birthplace. The 1900 census gives February 1856, a year earlier. The 1860 and 1870 census households remain leads for parentage because relationships were not recorded. His Texas death certificate no. 21353 gives 5 February 1857, Illinois, and death on 5 May 1932 in Houston; it identifies him as a widowed, retired groceryman, and the informant E. W. MAT_ALICE_WALKER.note: Original 1922 certificate no. 28867 records her mother as Addie Bruce (indexed Brace), born Illinois, and the informant as F. C. Livesay. Her father is indexed as Wm P. Walker; the handwritten surname is indistinct. The matching 1860/1870 household includes Abigail Walker, but her identity with Addie is unproved and no mother is linked. The birth field gives 11 January 1860; age 67 years, 9 months, 12 days implies 1855. The approximate 1859 census birth is retained without resolving those conflicts. A separate lead in the official Illinois marriage index records William F. Walker and Abigail Schanck in Washington County on 25 February 1852, volume A. This could concern the later census household, but the groom’s middle initial differs from Wm P. and the bride’s surname differs from Addie Bruce. The original marriage record has not been examined; neither this couple’s identity with the census household nor Schanck’s identity with Alice’s recorded mother is established. Her headstone in Pearland gives 11 January 1859, a fourth date alongside the 1855, 1859 and 1860 indications; the conflict remains open.

MAT_WILLIAM_P_WALKER.note: A 1922 death certificate for Alice May Livesay names Wm P. Walker as her father. A matching Alice appears in Wm P. and Abigail Walker’s 1860 and 1870 Illinois households; those censuses do not state relationships, and the identification is probable rather than certain. His stones at Beaucoup Cemetery read “W P Walker, Pvt, Ill Militia, Civil War, 1831–1919” and “Wm. P. Walker 1831–1919 / Abigail, his wife 1833–1923”; the full dates are from Find a Grave memorial 18750784. A 1922 death certificate for Alice May Livesay names Wm P. Walker as her father, and a matching Alice appears in Wm P. and Abigail Walker’s 1860 and 1870 Washington County households. Rev. James Walker and Etheldra Jane Ballard, proposed as his parents on Find a Grave, remain an unlinked lead.

MAT_WILLIAM_NELSON.note: The 1920 census identifies Audrey as his daughter and lists him as 49, born in Arkansas. A reproduced obituary names him as her father. Gravestone at Redland Cemetery: William A. Nelson, May 12, 1870 – Aug. 10, 1922. This matches the William A. Nelson, 46, of the 1916 Idabel marriage to Julia Myers and the 49-year-old Arkansas-born head of the 1920 household. Lead for parents: Aaron Burr Nelson (1815–1888) and Mary Elizabeth Anthony Nelson (1836–1916), per Find a Grave links only. Earlier children per memorial: Rosa Isabel Nelson Flowers (1894–1985) and Homer E. Nelson (1902–1999). Also recorded as William A. Nelson.

MAT_JULIA_ROBBINS.note: Audrey’s reproduced obituary supplies Robbins as Julia’s maiden name. The 1916 original Nelson–Myers marriage, 1920 Nelson household, 1930 Stevens household with daughter Audry, 1950 Stevens–Ratcliff marriage index and 1956 Ratcliff notice probably follow the same woman. Recorded ages imply conflicting birth years; the 1956 notice’s stated age conflicts with its 1873 birth date. Her parents remain unknown.

MAT_ALFREDA_WHITFIELD.note: Her obituary identifies her parents and daughter; the Choctaw Nation’s Biskinik identifies her grandmother and great-grandmother. The 1920 census identifies an Oliver L. Whitfield in the Oliver C. and Ida M. household; his identification as Lewis Oliver is probable.

MAT_LEWIS_WHITFIELD.note: Alfreda’s obituary names her father L. O. Whitfield. The 1920 census records an Oliver L. Whitfield with Oliver C. and Ida M. Whitfield; the identification with Lewis Oliver is probable and the name order differs. Ida May Merry Whitfield’s original February 1993 obituary names Lewis O. Whitfield of Golden as her surviving son, strengthening the mother-son connection, while the census name-order difference remains unresolved. Catherine Ouida Carroll’s original 2007 obituary names her deceased brother Oliver Lewis Whitfield; this separate notice supplies both names, but their order differs from Lewis Oliver used in other family accounts. Gravestone and military plaque at Wheelock Cemetery: Lewis O. Whitfield, Aug. 24, 1916 – Aug. 9, 2004, Pvt., U.S. Army Air Forces, World War II. Violet's 1962 obituary calls him Louis O. Whitfield, 46, and says he was a passenger in the wreck that killed her. Earlier notes still apply: the 1920 census lists Oliver L., and his sister's 2007 obituary calls him Oliver Lewis; the stone uses Lewis O.

MAT_VIOLET_BOX.dp: Oak Hill road near Golden, McCurtain County, Oklahoma
MAT_VIOLET_BOX.note: Alfreda’s obituary names Violet Box Whitfield as her mother. The 1930 census identifies Violet as Tyro Box’s daughter and lists Annie as her mother. Killed when the pickup she was driving overturned, per the McCurtain Gazette (August 1962, transcribed on Find a Grave). The obituary names her father T. S. Box of Millerton and her daughter Mrs. Larry Sandridge. Annie F. Box's 1959 obituary names her daughter Mrs. Louis Whitfield of Golden. The stone gives 22 September 1920 and the obituary 21 September.

MAT_IDA_MERRY.note: Her 1899 birth affidavit names Bessie Merry as her mother and Lewis Merry as her father. The February 1993 Bishinik obituary repeats 12 June 1898 and explicitly names her mother Bessie Durant Merry, father J. L. Merry and surviving son Lewis O. Whitfield. Her husband is Clinton O. C. Whitfield there, versus Oliver C. in the 1920 census. The husband’s name variants remain unresolved; the census son Oliver L. is a probable identification. The official final-roll index lists Ida May Merry, roll 15527, on Choctaw card 5754. Daughter Catherine Ouida Carroll’s 2007 obituary calls her parents Oliver Clinton and Ida May Merry Whitfield and her brother Oliver Lewis Whitfield, providing a second family account of the full names. The original 1903 letter names her with her parents and uses Lewis in the address and Louis in the body for her father, supporting those two spellings for the same applicant; the 1902 letter to J. L. shares the Glover address and D 128 reference with that response, supporting a probable identification, not proof or a full first-name expansion. Her death was reported in a February 1993 obituary; the exact date remains unverified. Elma Severn’s original December 2011 separate obituary names her parents Oliver Clinton and Ida Mae Merry Whitfield. Death date from her gravestone at Glover Cemetery (June 12, 1898 – Jan. 28, 1993). It agrees with the February 1993 obituary's “passed away Thursday” (28 January 1993 was a Thursday). The obituary also says she spent her childhood visiting her parents and attending Indian boarding schools, and that her younger son Omagene was killed in World War II. The Dawes index records her as 3/8 Choctaw by blood, roll 15527, card 5754. All earlier notes on name variants still apply.

MAT_OLIVER_C_WHITFIELD.note: The 1920 census names Oliver C. Whitfield as head of a household that includes son Oliver L.; identifying that child with Lewis Oliver Whitfield is probable. Ida’s 1993 obituary names her husband Clinton O. C. Whitfield, married in 1915 and deceased in 1941. The name-order and initials difference remains unresolved; no precise dates are adopted from that identification. Catherine Ouida Carroll’s original 2007 obituary names her father Oliver Clinton Whitfield, supporting that fuller name while the 1993 variant remains on record. A second child’s original obituary, Elma Severn’s in December 2011, also names her father Oliver Clinton Whitfield and mother Ida Mae Merry Whitfield. The display name follows these two separate child obituaries; identity with the census household remains probable, and the 1993 Clinton O. C. wording is retained. Gravestone at Glover Cemetery: O. C. (Clint) Whitfield, July 27, 1893 – Mar. 21, 1941. The stone reconciles Oliver C. (1920 census), Clinton O. C. (1993 obituary) and Oliver Clinton (children's obituaries). Leads, from Find a Grave only: born at Chapel Hill, Sevier County, Arkansas; parents William Franklin “Frank” Whitfield (1867–1944) and Emma Ward Whitfield (1874–1955). No parent link added.

MAT_LEWIS_MERRY.dp: Golden, McCurtain County, Oklahoma (buried Glover Cemetery)
MAT_LEWIS_MERRY.note: The 1899 affidavit names Lewis Merry as Bessie’s husband and Ida May Merry’s father. Ida’s 1993 obituary instead gives her father’s initials as J. L.; the official final-roll index lists Louis Merry, age 30, intermarried, roll 1363, on Choctaw card 5754. No parents are attached. The 24 October 1903 commissioner’s letter is addressed to Lewis Merry but calls the applicant Louis Merry in its body and names wife Bessie and child Ida May, directly supporting Lewis/Louis as spelling variants for the same applicant. The 6 October 1902 original is addressed to J. L. Merry at Glover under Choctaw D 128, matching the 1903 letter’s Glover address and 7-D 128 reference. This supports a probable identification of J. L. with Lewis/Louis, not proof or a full first-name expansion. The 18 January 1908 letter returns Louis and Bessie’s marriage documents; its date is not their marriage date. Gravestone at Glover Cemetery: “J. L. Louis Merry, Apr. 10, 1872 – July 1, 1932. Dear Papa, we miss you.” An undated newspaper marriage-license list names “Joshua L. Merry” of Glover marrying Mrs. Mattie Erwin. Together with the 1899–1908 Commission letters (Lewis/Louis/J. L., all at Glover), these make Joshua Louis probable. The Dawes index records him as an intermarried white citizen, age 30, roll 1363, card 5754. Leads from Find a Grave only: born Sevier County, Arkansas; parents John Calvin Merry and Eliza Jane McGregor; first postmaster at Glover; later marriages to Mattie Ervin (1908), Nancy Martha Gregg (1912) and Martha E. (1919). Also recorded as Joshua Louis “J. L.” Merry.

MAT_BESSIE_DURANT.dp: Golden, McCurtain County, Oklahoma (buried Denison Cemetery, Idabel)
MAT_BESSIE_DURANT.note: In her 1899 affidavit Bessie Merry, age 19, names herself as Ida May Merry’s mother. Ida’s February 1993 Bishinik obituary explicitly names her mother Bessie Durant Merry, strengthening that identity beyond the 2008 descendant notice. The official final-roll index lists Bessie Merry, age 21, roll 15526, on Choctaw card 5754. Her parents remain unknown and the original card needs examination. The 1903 commissioner’s letter names her as Louis Merry’s wife and Ida May’s mother. The Dawes final-roll index lists Bessie Merry, 21, 3/4 Choctaw by blood, roll 15526, card 5754. Her 1899 affidavit gives age 19, which fits a gravestone at Denison Cemetery, Idabel: “Bessie E. Kernell, Nov. 11, 1879 – Mar. 22, 1950.” Find a Grave links that stone to Ida May Merry Whitfield and gives a 1907 marriage to John Frank Kernell. The identification is probable. Her parents are not named in any source examined; enrollment card 5754 (father and mother columns) still needs to be read.

MAT_TYRO_BOX.note: The 1930 census records Violet as his daughter. A family-transcribed obituary names her father as T. S. Box; the identification of Tyro with T. S. is probable. The 1900 census names Alonzo and Emma as parents of a Tyro Box born in May 1888, Texas. A 1917 draft registration for Tyro Stevens Box also gives May 1888 and Texas and places him in McCurtain County. The 1930 census gives his birthplace as Oklahoma, so the match remains probable. His 1967 McCurtain Gazette obituary (transcribed on Find a Grave) gives his birth as 22 May 1888 at Pittsburg, Texas, and sixty years' residence in McCurtain County. It describes him as a retired engineer and Valliant Mason and names his brother Arch Box and sister Mrs. Byrd James. Violet's 1962 obituary names her father T. S. Box of Millerton, which confirms the T. S. identification. The draft card has Tyro Stevens; the obituary has Tyro Stephen. Parent link to Alonzo and Emma stays probable (1900 census plus matching birth month and year). Also recorded as Tyro Stephen Box.

MAT_ANNIE_BOX.note: The 1930 census identifies Annie as Violet’s mother. Her maiden name has not yet been established from an independent source. Her McCurtain Gazette obituary (30 December 1959, transcribed on Find a Grave) names her daughter Mrs. Louis Whitfield of Golden, her brothers Rob and Walter Logan and her sister Mrs. Bell Culpepper, and says she came from Mount Pleasant in 1906. The Wheelock Cemetery card file at the Broken Bow library names her parents as Dudley Logan and Annie Wedgeworth Logan. Sister Belle Logan Culpepper's memorial gives the same parents. The parent link is probable; no birth or marriage record naming them has been examined. Her stone appears to read 1958; the newspaper's 1959 is adopted. Also recorded as Annie F. Logan Box.

MAT_ALONZO_BOX.note: The 1900 census identifies him as father of Tyro Box, age twelve. The identification with the later Tyro in McCurtain County is probable. A family note on Tyro's Find a Grave memorial also calls Tyro “son of Alonzo & Emillie (Wilkerson) Box.”

MAT_EMMA_BOX.note: The 1900 census identifies Emma as mother of Tyro Box. A collaborative tree suggests Wilkerson as her maiden name; an independent record is needed. The 1900 census identifies Emma as mother of Tyro Box. A collaborative tree and a family note on Tyro's Find a Grave memorial (“Emillie (Wilkerson)”) both suggest Wilkerson as her maiden name; an independent original record is still needed.

MAT_CARYLON_LIVESAY_BARDWELL.note: The Pearland Historical Society’s July 2014 newsletter, p. 3, reports her death on 18 June in Carthage and names her parents as Lester and Barbara Livesay, brother Wayne Livesay and late husband Jimmy Bardwell. The identification with this family is probable; no birth date is supplied.

MAT_CATHERINE_OUIDA_WHITFIELD_CARROLL.note: Her May 2007 Bishinik obituary names her parents Oliver Clinton and Ida May Merry Whitfield and deceased brothers Omagene Clinton and Oliver Lewis Whitfield. She served as postmaster at Golden for 22 years and retired in 1990. The father and brother are probable identifications with the existing census-linked people; recorded name-order variants remain visible.

MAT_HATTIE_MYERS_KILGORE.note: Probable identification of William Nelson’s 1920 stepdaughter Hattie Myres with Hattie Myers Kilgore, whose memorial notice names her mother Mrs. Stevens and sister Audrey Nelson. The original certificate for Mrs. Gordon Kilgor records age 20 and 1909 birth year, with day/month and parent information unobtainable. The memorial instead gives 23 September 1906; unresolved. Her father remains unknown.

MAT_NONA_MYERS_ALFORD.note: The original Broken Bow News of 7 March 1940 identifies Nona Alford as Julia Stevens’s daughter and Mrs. L. L. Sandridge’s sister. Identifying the latter as Audrey is strongly supported by her husband, son Larry and family records. The 1919 marriage and daughters’ Social Security entries supply Myers as Nona’s earlier surname. Her father remains unassigned. A proposed later Kinley identity has not been established.

MAT_WESLEY_E_ALFORD.note: The 1919 original marriage names Wesley E. Alford and Nona Myers. Their daughters’ Social Security entries name Wesley, or Wesly, E. Alford as father. A 1940 original Tulsa marriage names the same couple and gives Wesley’s age as 47; identifying it as the earlier pair is probable.

MAT_MABEL_ALFORD_CHIDESTER.note: Social Security NUMIDENT indexes Mabel Alford Chidester, with a later Crowl alias, and names Nona A. Myers and Wesly E. Alford as her parents. The 1940 Camden census names her as Edwin Chidester’s wife. She is the strong match for the unnamed Mrs. Edwin Chidester in the March 1940 family visit. Her 1938 marriage records age 20, conflicting with the 1920 birth date, which would make her 18.

MAT_GERALDINE_ALFORD_FORKNER.note: Her Social Security NUMIDENT entry names Nona A. Myers and Wesley E. Alford as parents and supplies the Forkner alias. A 1992 obituary index identifies Mabel A. Crowl as her sister; the original obituary has not been examined.

MAT_CARL_C_PHILLIPS.note: Named as Barbara Phillips Livesay’s father in her 1995 obituary, which says that her parents had died before her. His dates and residence have not been examined.

MAT_BEULAH_TURNER_PHILLIPS.note: Named as Barbara Phillips Livesay’s mother, “Beulah Turner Phillips,” in her 1995 obituary, which says that her parents had died before her. Her dates have not been examined.

MAT_DUDLEY_LOGAN.note: Named as Annie F. Box's father in the Wheelock Cemetery card file (via her Find a Grave memorial). Her 1959 obituary's Logan siblings match his children on Find a Grave. Buried Masonic Cemetery, Mount Pleasant, Texas. His memorial says he came to Titus County from Greene County, Alabama; the parents it names (James Clement Logan and Martha Calhoun) are leads and not adopted.

MAT_ANNIE_WEDGEWORTH_LOGAN.note: Named as Annie F. Box's mother (“Annie Wedgeworth Logan”) in the Wheelock Cemetery card file via Find a Grave. Her years (1846–1923) come from Find a Grave family links and have not been checked against her own memorial or an original record.

MAT_OMAGENE_WHITFIELD.dp: Normandy, France (missing; Tablets of the Missing, Normandy American Cemetery)
MAT_OMAGENE_WHITFIELD.note: Ida's 1993 obituary: “Her younger son, Omagene Whitfield, was killed during World War II.” Catherine Carroll's 2007 obituary names her deceased brother Omagene Clinton Whitfield. Tec 5, 300th Engineer Combat Battalion, service no. 38466149, died 19 June 1944; memorialized on the Tablets of the Missing. Presence aboard LST-523 (mined that day) is probable, not proven.
